post.summary:
Asks for a one-time code to a customer's number, by SMS or on WhatsApp (SMS behind it).
The caller pays first: the source's and the device's allowances are counted before the
number is read. The answer is the same three facts whether or not the number has an
account. A code again within a minute for the same purpose is `otp_too_soon`; past the
number's ten a day, the device's five or the source's two hundred an hour, `otp_daily_limit`,
never saying which.

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: `validation_failed`: `invalid_mobile` or `not_a_mobile` on `/mobile`, or a malformed device

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the number's market does not admit sign-in, or the market named is not configured

503.description: A store or the message provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Completes a registration: the profile the platform can stand behind (a given name, the
number proved, an optional email) and, optionally, a first address, written at once with a
session. The market's gate is consulted again. A number another device registered meanwhile
signs in to that account (`existing_account`), this draft dropped. A registration token
past its thirty minutes, or anything that is not one, is `registration_expired`.

200.description: Registered and signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh cookie is set

400.description: `validation_failed`: the name, the email, `date_of_birth_future`, `too_young`, `terms_not_accepted`, the address (`postal_code_invalid`, `pin_far_from_address`, `invalid_mobile`), `delivery_required`

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the market closed to sign-in meanwhile

post.summary:
Verifies a customer's code. A registered number is signed in on the customer surface,
delivered as stated (the Storefront's refresh token in the `zg_refresh_customer` cookie,
the app's in the body); a new number receives a registration context, valid thirty
minutes, and nothing about it is stored. Every failure (an unknown, expired or used code, a
code issued for another purpose, too many attempts, a wrong code) answers the same
`otp_invalid`.

200.description: Signed in, or a registration to complete; with cookie delivery a signed-in session sets the refresh cookie

403.description: `account_blocked`: the account is blocked; the detail says how to reach support

202.description: A code is on its way to the new address

400.description: Malformed address, or the account's own

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

delete.summary: Cancels a pending change: the old address stands and the code sent is useless.

post.summary:
Confirms the change with the code sent to the new address: it signs in from now, the old
address is told, and every other session ends while this one continues. A new address
another account holds is refused, but only once its code passed.

Requests a one-time code by email or SMS for the Partner console or the Agent app. Always
accepted for a well-formed identifier, so nothing reveals whether an account exists; the
user is created on the first verification. A second code inside a minute, more than ten a
day for one identifier or two hundred an hour from one source are refused.

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: Malformed identifier; `audience_required` on `/audience` without one, `audience_not_allowed` for Mission Control

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: the number's country is not accepting sign-in

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Exchanges a one-time code for a session on the surface the code was asked for. Five wrong
codes lock the challenge (`too_many_attempts`); wrong codes also count in the sign-in
throttle. An unknown, used or expired challenge is `code_expired`.

200.description: Signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh token is set as a cookie

202.description: The code was right and two-step sign-in is on: send an authenticator or recovery code to `POST /v1/auth/two-step/verify`

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` and `delivery_required` on `/delivery` without them; `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience`

429.description: `too_many_attempts`, or `too_many_requests` while the sign-in throttle holds the identifier or the source

post.summary:
Sets the password of the signed-in user. Once a password is set, the current one is
required even inside a valid session (`forbidden` when missing or wrong, counted in the
sign-in throttle). A change ends every session of the user on every surface, this one
included (its cookie is cleared), and is announced to the user's email; a first password
ends the other sessions.

204.description: Password set; after a change every session has ended

403.description: `forbidden`: the user has a password and `current_password` is missing or wrong; `step_up_required`: a first password needs a fresh proof (`POST /v1/auth/step-up`)

post.summary:
Sets a new password through a link, at the console it was asked from. Every session of the
user ends; two-step sign-in still applies to the next sign-in. A refused password leaves the
link unused.

204.description: Password set; sign in with it

410.description: `link_invalid`: expired, used, replaced, or asked at the other console

post.summary:
Asks for a password link. The answer is always 202, whether or not the address signs in at
this console: when it does, a link is emailed that works once, for thirty minutes, and only
at this console, and earlier links stop working. Five asks in fifteen minutes per address
and per caller are allowed; beyond that nothing is sent and the answer is the same.

400.description: Malformed email, or `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience` (the Agent app has no password link)

post.summary:
Email and password sign-in to one surface. Every failure before the password is proven,
and a surface the account may not enter, is the same `authentication_failed`, in about the
same time; five failures in fifteen minutes for one identifier on one surface, or from one
source, lock it for the rest of the window (`too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`).

200.description: Signed in; with cookie delivery the refresh token is set as a cookie. A Mission Control session of platform staff without a second factor reaches the two-step set-up only (`two_step_setup_required`)

202.description: The password was right and two-step sign-in is on: send an authenticator or recovery code to `POST /v1/auth/two-step/verify`

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` and `delivery_required` on `/delivery` without them; `audience_not_allowed` on `/audience`

429.description: `too_many_requests`: the throttle holds the identifier or the source

post.summary:
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token on the family's surface,
delivered as the family was created whatever the request carries. Clients with cookie
delivery send `audience` to name the cookie; clients with body delivery send
`refresh_token`; neither is `audience_required`. The token spent by the latest rotation is
forgiven for fifteen seconds and answers the same successor; an older one revokes the whole
family. Every refusal is the same 401, and clears the cookie. A customer session whose
market closed sign-in meanwhile is `sign_in_closed` and kept: it renews once the market
reopens.

requestBody.description: The refresh token, or the surface whose cookie carries it

200.description: New tokens; with cookie delivery a new cookie

400.description: Malformed body; `audience_required` on `/audience` with neither a refresh token nor a surface

401.description: No token, an unknown or spent token, or a family that ended (signed out, revoked, past its idle or absolute limit, or a surface the user may no longer enter)

403.description: `account_blocked`: a customer whose account support blocked; the detail says how to reach support, and the session stays ended

409.description: `sign_in_closed`: a customer session whose market closed sign-in; the session is kept, the cookie too

post.summary:
Mints a service token for a background job (workers, the simulator, CI) from its bootstrap
credential: audience `service`, the credential's one job, at most an hour. A service token
holds no memberships and is refused by every human surface; only the routes a job may call
accept it.

Ends the current session, or with `everywhere` every session of the user on every surface
(a customer's `everywhere` is every customer session: the storefront reaches no Partner
console or Mission Control session), and clears the cookie, unconditionally: the answer is 204 whether or not the session still
existed. The session is the bearer token's, or the one the cookie (named by `audience`) or
the body's `refresh_token` belongs to, so a client whose access token expired can still end
it. A view-as (impersonation) token signs nobody out (`403`): the session is ended from
Mission Control.

204.description: Signed out (or nothing to end); the refresh cookie is cleared

403.description: A view-as (impersonation) token, which signs nobody out (`forbidden`)

post.summary:
Proves the signed-in person afresh, with exactly one of: the password, an authenticator
code, or a code from `POST /v1/auth/step-up/code`. The proof stands ten minutes, for this
session only; sensitive acts refused as `step_up_required` pass after it.

400.description: Not exactly one proof, or `code_invalid` on `/code`

403.description: `forbidden`: the password or authenticator code is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary:
Sends a one-time code proving the signed-in person to the account's own email or phone,

202.description: A code is on its way

400.description: The account has no such address

429.description: `too_many_requests`: a code was sent less than a minute ago

503.description: A store or the delivery provider is unavailable

post.summary:
Turns two-step sign-in on with a code from the app, and returns ten recovery codes, shown
once. A Mission Control session that reached the set-up only reaches everything from now.
Turns the user's own two-step sign-in off, only after the password again.

403.description: `forbidden`: the password is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary: Replaces the recovery codes with ten new ones, only after the password again.

200.description: The new codes; the old ones no longer work

403.description: `forbidden`: the password is wrong (it counts in the throttle)

post.summary:
Starts setting up an authenticator: a new secret, as text and as an `otpauth://` link the
console shows as a QR code, issued as "ZippyGo Mission Control" or "ZippyGo Partner
console". Sign-in does not change until `POST /v1/auth/two-step/confirm` proves it.

200.description: The secret to add to the app

503.description: `two_step_unavailable`: this deployment holds no two-step key; or a store is unavailable

post.summary:
Exchanges the second step of a sign-in for the session: six digits from the authenticator
app (a code already used, or an earlier one, is refused) or a recovery code (once, with or
without its dash, in either case). Five wrong codes end the challenge; wrong codes count in
the sign-in throttle. The session goes where the sign-in asked, delivered as it stated.

429.description: `too_many_attempts`, or `too_many_requests` while the throttle holds the identifier or the source

503.description: A store is unavailable, or no two-step key is configured

configuration and the Locations it is switched on at.

agents.description:
The agents holding a membership in it, for delivery and field Services; `null` for
product sales or when the fleet cannot say.

awaiting.description: The documents it waits for, while `awaiting_documents`.

blockers.description:
What stops it trading, each with its code: `service_disabled`, `document_missing`,
`document_pending`, `document_rejected`, `document_expired`, `not_in_plan`,
`partner_not_active`, `switched_on_nowhere`, `no_agents`.

config.description:
Kind-specific settings: `ProductSalesConfig`, `FieldServiceConfig` or `DeliveryConfig`;
members the platform does not know are kept as sent.

created_by.description: Who registered it; `null` for the step 1 rows and the seed.

everywhere.description: `true` when it is switched on at every Location of the Partner, present and future.

location_ids.description: The Locations it is switched on at (every open Location when `everywhere`).

name.description: Its name, defaulting to its kind.

pricing_version.description: The current pricing version, for a delivery Service that has one.

status_reason.description: Why it is in its status, when platform staff or a plan change set it.

trading.description:
`true` when it trades somewhere now: enabled, in the plan, the Partner active, switched
on at a Location, and with agents for an agent-based kind.

updated_at.description: When the service was last changed.

version.description: The version, raised by one on every change.

default_for_country.description: Whether it is its country's default.

fenced_descendants.description: How many fenced service areas sit beneath it.

kind.description: A label only; immutable because it appears in history.

parent_id.description: The parent node; `null` at the top of a country.

path.description: The materialised path every descendant embeds.

serves.description: Whether the area serves anybody: fenced and effectively active.

slug.description: The slug, immutable; part of the path.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone, one the country spans.

ServiceArea.description: A node of the geography tree, the `ServiceArea` schema.

oneOf.description: The fence, when the area serves itself.

parent_id.description: The parent, or omitted at the top of the country.

time_zone.description: Time zone; the parent's, else the country's first, when omitted.

ServiceAreaRef.description: A reference to a service area in another record's answer.

ServiceAtLocation.description: A Service at one Location, the `ServiceAtLocation` schema.

everywhere.description: Whether it is on there because it is on everywhere.

oneOf.description: For a field Service: its bookable area, hours and slots there, defaults filled in.

switched_on.description: Whether the Service is switched on there.

config.description:
Its configuration by kind: `ProductSalesConfig`, `FieldServiceConfig` or
`DeliveryConfig`; `{}` when absent.

enabled.description:
`false` registers it disabled; enabled by default, awaiting documents while its kind
needs some not approved.

everywhere.description:
Switched on at every Location, present and future; the default when `location_ids` is
absent.

location_ids.description: The Locations to switch it on at; `[]` switches it on nowhere.

name.description: Its name, 1 to 100 characters; the kind's when absent.

reason.description: Why; required of platform staff acting for the Partner.

ServiceKind.description: The kind of service a partner runs.

ServiceList.description: The `ServiceList` schema: the registry of a Partner.

kinds.description:
Every kind and where it stands for the Partner: enabled, awaiting documents, disabled,
available, or not in the plan with the plan that includes it.

plan.description: The plan in force, with the kinds it includes.

reason.description: Why; required of platform staff acting for the Partner.

oneOf.description:
For a field Service, its area, hours and slots at the Location, defaults filled in for
absent members; absent for any other kind.

ServicePolicy.description:
A policy layer's fields, the `ServicePolicy` schema. Every member is optional: `null`
defers to the layer above; zero is a decision.

fee_by_distance.description: Fee by distance from the Location, a ladder of bands in metres.

fee_by_order_value.description: Fee by order value, a ladder of bands in minor units.

minimum_order_value.description: Minimum order value in minor units.

prescription_fee.description: Prescription fee per dispensed line, in minor units.

service_fee_ceiling.description: Ceiling of the service fee in minor units.

service_fee_floor.description: Floor of the service fee in minor units.

service_fee_percent.description: Platform service fee as a percentage, 0 to 100.

small_order_fee.description: Fee charged below the minimum instead of refusal, in minor units.

ServiceStatus.description:
Whether a Service is switched on: enabled and trading where it is switched on, enabled
but awaiting the documents its kind needs (configurable, not trading), or disabled with
its configuration kept.

access_token.description: The access token: a JWT of audience `service` for the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

expires_in.description: Seconds until it expires (at most an hour); mint another from the credential then.

job.description: The one job the token may do.

turnaround_hours.description: Turnaround in hours, for pickup-and-return work.

fields.description: Typed extra fields, from the service field catalogue.

turnaround_hours.description: Turnaround in hours, required for pickup-and-return work.

ServiceUpdateBody.description:
Request body of `PATCH /v1/partners/{partner_id}/services/{kind}`, the `ServiceUpdate`
schema: absent members are kept.

everywhere.description: `true` switches it on at every Location; `false` keeps it on where it is, one by one.

location_ids.description: Switches it on at exactly these Locations.

reason.description: Why; required of platform staff acting for the Partner.

oneOf.description: `enabled` or `disabled`; disabling keeps the configuration, re-enabling restores it.

name.description: A new name; kept when omitted.

reason.description: Why; required of platform staff acting for the Partner.

status.description:
`enabled` or `disabled`; enabling lands in `awaiting_documents` while the kind needs
documents not approved.

Serviceability.description:
Whether a pin can be served, the `Serviceability` schema: what an order will check, asked
before a pin is confirmed.

reason.description: Why not, as a sentence a screen may show as is; `null` when serviceable.
reason.example: Orders are paused in this country at the moment.

serviceable.description: Inside a serving zone, every ancestor active, the country active and accepting orders.

oneOf.description: The zone the pin lies in, when it lies in one.

ServicesBlock.description: What a bookable service of a type collects, the `ServicesBlock` schema.

cancellation_notice.description: Whether a cancellation notice in hours is stated.

deposit.description: Whether a deposit may be taken.

duration.description: Whether a service states its duration.

SessionClient.description: The kind of client holding a session, the `SessionClient` schema.

Setting.description: A setting as served, the `Setting` schema.

updated_at.description: When the stored value was set.

value.description: The value in force: the override when one is stored and in range, else the default.

items.description: Every setting with the value in force.

value.description: The value, within the declared bounds.

oneOf.description: The surface whose cookie to read and clear, for clients whose delivery is `cookie`.

everywhere.description:
End every session of the user on every surface, not only this one; for a customer
session, every customer session.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token, for clients whose delivery is `body` and whose access token expired.

Signal.description:
A signal, the data of a `signal` frame and the `Signal` schema. Clients refetch on a signal
rather than apply it; one holding a version equal to or newer than `version` may skip.

channel.description: The channel the signal belongs to.

status.description: Its new status, where it has one.

version.description: Its version, which only rises per aggregate.

SignedLink.description: A signed link to a restricted file, the `SignedLink` schema.

url.description: The link; works until `expires_at` and never again.

SlotHours.description: Hours of the week a campaign slot shows, in the service area's own clock.

to.description: Until this local time; `00:00` means midnight at the close of the day.

SlotLink.description: What a campaign slot links to, the `SlotLink` schema.

targets.description:
The target ids: exactly one for a Vertical, Partner or campaign; one or more Location
ids for `locations`; one or more `location_id/product_id` for `products`.

SnapshotFrame.description:
Data of a `snapshot` frame: the current facts of a channel whose frames carry facts, the
`AgentsSnapshot` schema.

agents.description: Every agent the channel covers, at the time the stream opened.

SourcedAmount.description: An amount in minor units with the layer that supplied it, the `SourcedAmount` schema.

source.description: Whose decision it was: the layer and the version that supplied the value.

SourcedException.description: An exception with the layer that declared it.

SourcedFlag.description: A yes or no with the layer that supplied it, the `SourcedFlag` schema.

source.description: Whose decision it was: the layer and the version that supplied the value.

SourcedLadder.description: A fee ladder with the layer that supplied it, the `SourcedLadder` schema.

source.description: Whose decision it was: the layer and the version that supplied the value.

SourcedRate.description: A percentage with the layer that supplied it, the `SourcedRate` schema.

source.description: Whose decision it was: the layer and the version that supplied the value.

StaffAgentRating.description: One rating as staff read it, the `StaffAgentRating` schema.

tags.description: Its tags.

oneOf.description: The share among their delivery ratings.

next_cursor.description: The next page's cursor.

Standing.description: The Partner console's view of its registration and standing, the `PartnerStanding` schema.

activation.description: What activation needs, with every blocker.

oneOf.description: The payout account, masked; `null` until stated.

payouts_may_go.description: Whether the next payout may go out now: the account verified and any hold over.

requirements.description:
Every document the Partner must have on file and where each stands: its review, its
expiry, and what it does to trading.

status_reason.description: Why it is in that status, shown while it is suspended.

withheld_permissions.description: The permissions withheld from the Partner's entitlement envelope.

StandingSummary.description: What the directory row carries beside a Partner, the `PartnerStandingSummary` schema.

can_trade.description: Whether the Partner can trade now: active, and no document has stopped every Location.

documents_missing.description: Required documents missing, rejected or expired.

nobody_can_sign_in.description: `true` when nobody can sign in to the Partner, which platform staff should notice.

runs.description: The kinds of Service it runs: those with a Service enabled or awaiting documents.

no_fee_sentence.description: That the platform charged no fee.

standing.description: Where the money stands, in a sentence.

version.description: The version.

StatementActor.description: Who made a move, the `StatementActor` schema.

kind.description: The clock, the provider or staff.

name.description: The operator's name, in Mission Control only.

StatementActorKind.description: Who made a move, the `StatementActorKind` schema.

StatementDay.description: One day of a week, the `StatementDay` schema.

total.description: The day's part of the total.

StatementDocumentKind.description: A document of a locked week, the `StatementDocumentKind` schema.

delivery_charges.description: Delivery charges that are the Location's.

fee_gst.description: GST on the fee as the invoice bills it.

promotions.description: What the Partner paid towards its promotions.

partner_gets.description: What the Partner got for it.

plan.description: The policy layer of the rate.

refunds.description: Refunds of it in the week.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page.

StatementStanding.description: Where the money stands in a sentence, the `StatementStanding` schema.

A status change with its reason, the `StatusChange` schema. The reason is required where

A variant's stock: in stock, out of stock until switched back, or sold out until 00:00
in the store's clock.

oneOf.description: The minimum order from the resolved policy, when one is set.

offline_message.description: What the store says while it is offline.

preparation_minutes.description: The minutes the store quotes for preparation now.

oneOf.description:
The store's rating, the share of thumbs up with how many reviews ("72% (18)"); `null`
with no reviews or when it takes none, rather than 0%.

shelves.description: The Vertical's categories (shelves) the store sits on.

state.description: Open, shut by the clock, or offline.

When the state changes: closing time when open, opening time when shut, back-at time
when offline; `null` when unknown.

zone_id.description: The zone the store is in.

A Vertical's stores as cards, the `StoreCardList` schema: open stores lead, then those

name without one.

open.description: The open windows; empty is closed.

UploadGrant.description: A grant to post one file straight to the destination, the `UploadGrant` schema.

content_type.description: The exact content type the destination accepts for this grant.

fields.description: The form fields to send, every one of them, before the file part.

file_field.description: The name of the file part, sent last.

key.description: The object key the destination will hold the file under; confirm with it.

max_bytes.description: The largest size the destination accepts for this grant, in bytes.

User.description: A person, the `User` schema: who they are, never what they may do (that is a membership).

display_name.description: The name the user is shown under, `null` until set.

email.description: Email address, normalised; `null` for phone-only users.

phone.description: Phone number in E.164; `null` for email-only users.

VariantInput.description:
A variant as sent, the `CatalogVariantInput` schema. `selection` keys and values may be ids
or the English names of the axis and the value.

id.description: Keeps the variant, its stock and its price history.

mrp.description: The MRP printed on the pack.

price.description: The price in minor units of the store's currency, tax included.

quantity.description: How many are on hand, where inventory is tracked.

selection.description: The value chosen on each axis; empty for the default variant.

oneOf.description: The GST class; `null` inherits the Vertical's default.

VehicleKind.description: A vehicle a delivery Service runs.

VehicleType.description: A vehicle type with what it carries, the `VehicleType` schema.

VerificationOutcome.description: How a verified code turned out, the `CustomerVerificationOutcome` schema.

image_asset_id.description: The image shown on its tile.

VerticalCategory.description: A category of a Vertical, the `VerticalCategory` schema.

id.description: Identity that outlives renames and reorders.

VerticalCategoryInput.description: One category as sent, the `VerticalCategoryInput` schema; the id is kept when given.

id.description: The identity to keep; a fresh one when omitted.

VerticalIdsBody.description: Request body of the Vertical set and order routes, the `VerticalIds` schema.

asset_id.description: The image asset, or `null` to clear.

VerticalKind.description: Whether a Vertical lists product sales or field services.

VerticalOffer.description: A Vertical as a service area offers it, the `VerticalOffer` schema.

inherited_from.description: The ancestor whose declaration reaches here, when inherited.

offered.description: Whether the Vertical trades here: declared here or inherited, and the Vertical active.

offered_here.description: Whether this service area declares the offer itself.

items.description: The Verticals as the area offers them, in its order.

held.description: What open orders hold, both balances together.

updated_at.description: When it last changed; `null` for a Wallet that never moved.

version.description: Rises with every entry; the `ETag`.

WalletApplication.description: The Wallet as checkout applies it, the `WalletApplication` schema.

applies.description: What it pays of this order.

available.description: What other orders do not hold.

WalletBalance.description: The Wallet at checkout, the `WalletBalance` schema.

WalletBalanceKind.description: One of the Wallet's two balances.

WalletBalances.description: Both balances at a moment, the `WalletBalances` schema.

WalletCorrectionRequest.description: Body of a correction, the `WalletCorrectionRequest` schema.

amount_minor.description: Positive adds, negative takes away; never zero.

note.description: Support's note, never shown to the customer.

reason.description: Why, in at most 40 characters the customer reads.

WalletCreditRequest.description: Body of a credit, the `WalletCreditRequest` schema.

amount_minor.description: The amount in paise, at least 100.

reason.description: Why, in at most 40 characters the customer reads.

WalletEntry.description: One entry of a Wallet, the `WalletEntry` schema.

amount.description: What it added to the balance (negative takes away).

by_user_id.description: The member who gave or corrected it, for Mission Control.

held.description: What it added to what orders hold.

note.description: A credit's message to the customer; a correction's note for Mission Control only.

WalletEntryPage.description: A page of entries, the `WalletEntryPage` schema.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page.

WalletPayer.description: Who pays for a credit, the `WalletPayer` schema.

WalletStatement.description: A calendar month of the Wallet, the `WalletStatement` schema.

closing.description: The balances when it ended, or now for the month under way.

entries.description: Every entry of the month, oldest first.

opening.description: The balances when the month began.

WalletSubBalance.description: One balance of the Wallet, the `WalletSubBalance` schema.

held.description: What open orders hold of it.

WalletTopUpRequest.description: Body of a top-up, the `WalletTopUpRequest` schema.

return_url.description: Where the provider's page sends the customer back.

save_method.description: Save the card or UPI ID once paid.

saved_method_id.description: A saved card or UPI ID.

upi_id.description: The UPI ID a collect request goes to.

entries.description: The withdrawal entries, one per source.

refunds.description: The refunds sent back to the sources.

WalletWithdrawalRequest.description: Body of a withdrawal, the `WalletWithdrawalRequest` schema.

Window.description: An open window of a day, the `Window` schema.

to.description: Closes at; `00:00` means midnight at the close of the day.

Workflow.description: The workflow of a field service.

WorkflowStep.description: A step of a task's workflow, the `WorkflowStep` schema.

done_at.description: When it was recorded on the device.

required.description: Whether the task cannot complete without it.

ZoneRef.description: A zone by id and name, the `ZoneRef` schema.

Bearer.description: An access token issued by the sign-in operations: a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519), valid for 15 minutes, verifiable with the keys at /.well-known/jwks.json.
